result.message: Reviewed the selected operator selu_ (subject cec7c025...) end to end: the frozen catalog Definition, oracle, 24 correctness and 12 timing workloads, the evaluation contract, the optimize ledger plus its best kernel (round 1), and the review_tests evidence. The best kernel (.best_kernel.py, identical to best_code in the ledger/optimize output) is a genuine FlagGems-style in-place Triton implementation: it computes scale*where(x>0, x, alpha*(exp(x)-1)) in fp32 and casts back to the input dtype, stores to the same pointer (no aliasing violation), returns the same tensor, defines run(A) with the Definition's parameter name, and contains no torch.ops.aten / torch.selu_ fallback, no dispatcher or reference replacement, no host synchronization and no environment mutation. Mutation + return-alias effects declared in definition.json are honoured. The candidate validated 36/36 workloads with abs_err/rel_err 0.0, so correctness is not in question for the frozen case set. Two substantive code limitations remain: (a) the non-contiguous path decomposes only 4 padded dimensions, so rank>4 non-contiguous inputs compute wrong offsets (torch.selu_ supports arbitrary rank); (b) the candidate is slower than the reference on every one of the 12 timing workloads (geo_mean 0.1271, min speedup 0.0820, 6.5x-12.2x slower), and the profile-measured BLOCK_SIZE=8192 retune (605 -> 176 us on 4096x4096) was never adopted. The review_tests stage recorded an explicit orchestration skip for a different subject sha (9f57f199...), so no test-contract review of this candidate exists; I reviewed the Definition/oracle/workloads directly instead and found no candidate-injection or reference-circularity defect. All code findings are advisory per policy.
